_about: Pre-registered data scope (Phase 1). Committed before any download. Chosen by the user on 2026-11-21 from three options shown with record counts and download sizes.
recall_window: all recalls for the product codes (no date filter), so recalls before and after the report window can be lined up with report trends

LPH.device_name: Prosthesis, Hip, Semi-Constrained, Metal/Polymer, Porous Uncemented
LPH.why: hip implant: core orthopedic product line at companies like Stryker; recall-rich

JWH.device_name: Prosthesis, Knee, Patellofemorotibial, Semi-Constrained, Cemented, Polymer/Metal/Polymer
JWH.why: cemented knee implant: most recalls of all candidates (985 all time)

MBH.why: uncemented knee: pairs with JWH to compare fixation types

LWP.why: pacemaker: core product line at companies like Medtronic; a second device family to compare against

LZG.why: insulin pump: electromechanical + software failure modes, different from implants

expected_counts_at_registration._source: openFDA server-side totals queried 2026-11-21 (event data last_updated 2026-11-11). openFDA refreshes weekly, so the download records the server total at download time and compares against that.

excluded.FRN: infusion pumps: 1,111,589 reports in 2022-2024, of which 888,020 in 2022 and 1,012,959 (2022-2023) from one manufacturer (CareFusion SD). Would multiply the download by ~7 and let one manufacturer's bulk reporting dominate every count. Recorded as a possible later extension.
excluded.QFG, OZP: insulin dosing systems with 590k and 430k reports: same size problem; LZG represents insulin pumps
excluded.DXY, NVZ, LWJ, KWY: smaller pacemaker / hip codes; kept out to keep one code per device type except knees (JWH + MBH)
